clue.text: Judge produced by wise men — sound, we hear

parts.note: the Magi are the wise men of the Nativity story

indicators.note: we hear says a word is to be taken by how it is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: a sound is a narrow sea channel, also called a strait

explanation.surface: Asking what a judge is made of, with talk of wise men and sound reasoning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like an adjective meaning sensible, but it is a noun: a narrow sea channel. 'we hear' asks for a word that sounds like that one but is spelt differently.
explanation.definitionFit: A magistrate is a minor judicial officer who tries lesser cases in court.

clue.text: Drip landed on the French head-dress

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second, as if landed on it

parts.note: a drip is a feeble, spineless person, a wimp
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Water drips onto a French headdress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drip' reads as water but means a feeble person.
explanation.definitionFit: A wimple is a cloth covering for the head and neck worn by medieval women and some nuns.

clue.text: Boot's last hobnail worked loose, in the event

indicators.note: a hobnail worked loose has come out of place, so the letters are rearranged
last points to the final letter of the word boot

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A nail in a boot heel comes loose during some event.
explanation.walkthrough: T, the last letter of 'Boot's', joins HOBNAIL and the eight letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The biathlon is an Olympic sporting contest combining cross-country skiing and rifle shooting.

clue.text: Painter's first application for elementary sort of work

explanation.surface: A decorator's undercoat compared with a beginner's piece of writing.
explanation.definitionFit: A primer is both the first coat of paint put on a surface and an introductory schoolbook.

clue.text: Hurt mitts are bruised

indicators.note: bruised suggests something knocked out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone's mittened hands have been injured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are' is part of the fodder: MITTS ARE gives eight letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To mistreat is to abuse or treat badly, which causes harm.

clue.text: Pawn expected to capture pawn

indicators.note: capturing a piece holds it inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: something due is expected, as a train due at noon
P is the chess abbreviation for pawn

explanation.surface: A chess move: one pawn is set to take another.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess picture hides that the first 'Pawn' is the definition, a person used by others.
explanation.definitionFit: A pawn in the figurative sense is someone manipulated by others, a gullible victim.

clue.text: One bird returns to normally dry valley

indicators.note: returns tells us to read the pieces backwards

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
a daw, or jackdaw, is a bird of the crow family

explanation.surface: A single bird flies back to a desert valley.
explanation.definitionFit: A wadi is a riverbed in arid North Africa or Arabia that carries water only after rain.

clue.text: Despotic, very contained, closed to persuasion

indicators.note: contained means one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: despotic and imperious both mean domineering and overbearing

explanation.surface: A tyrant, very self-contained, will not be talked round.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is impervious cannot be affected or influenced, so argument does not get through.

clue.text: At sea, master pleaded for ship

indicators.note: at sea means confused or disordered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Out on the ocean, the captain begged for a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'master' and 'pleaded' together give the thirteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A paddle steamer is a vessel driven by steam-powered paddle wheels.

clue.text: Stupid changes editor questioned

indicators.note: changes says the letters of stupid are rearranged

explanation.surface: An editor alters a silly piece of text.
explanation.definitionFit: Something disputed is challenged or called into doubt.

clue.text: Grouse, first seen in Magnolia state

indicators.note: the first letter seen in a word, here magnolia

parts.note: to state is to say or utter

explanation.surface: A game bird first spotted in the Magnolia State, Mississippi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grouse' wants to be the bird, but here it is the verb to grumble; 'Magnolia state' is not Mississippi but an M and a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To grouse is to complain in a low grumbling voice.

clue.text: Close behind and under control

explanation.surface: A dog trained to stay close behind and do as told.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog brought to heel walks just behind its owner and is obedient, so both senses apply.

clue.text: Society, we hear, is started by this generosity

indicators.note: we hear says the phrase is taken by its spoken sound

parts.note: the word Society begins with a capital, that is a big, letter S, so this is a large S

explanation.surface: Society, rumour has it, owes its beginnings to someone's kindness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Society' begins with a capital S, a 'large S'; 'we hear' says that spoken phrase sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Largesse is liberal giving of money or gifts, open-handedness.

clue.text: Firm endlessly produces yields

indicators.note: endlessly removes the final letter of a word

parts.note: firm and sure both mean secure and steady
to render is to produce or provide

explanation.surface: A business keeps turning out crops or profits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts the E from SURE to give SUR.
explanation.definitionFit: To surrender is to give up or hand over, as an army yields.

clue.text: This type always manages

parts.note: reads as praise for a capable coper, but describes someone whose job is managing affairs

explanation.surface: Praise for the sort of person who always copes.
explanation.definitionFit: An administrator is a person whose job is to manage an organisation or business.

clue.text: Channel for current crime, all broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A news bulletin of present-day crime, all of it on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' reads as up-to-date but is the flow of water.
explanation.definitionFit: A millrace is the channel carrying water to turn a mill wheel.

clue.text: By the way, it is

parts.note: reads as a conversational aside, but literally describes what lies beside a road

explanation.surface: A speaker's offhand aside, as in by the way, it is.
explanation.definitionFit: The roadside is the strip of land along the edge of a road, literally by the way.

clue.text: Film clip Elle reviewed

indicators.note: reviewed read as re-viewed, viewed again in a new order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A movie clip featuring Elle is critiqued.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film' looks like a movie but is a thin skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A pellicle is a thin skin or membrane on a surface.

clue.text: Split stick

explanation.surface: Two words that pull in opposite directions.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleave has opposite senses: to chop apart and to adhere closely.

clue.text: South wind's endlessly harsh

indicators.note: endlessly removes the final letter of a word

parts.note: harsh and austere both mean severe and stern

explanation.surface: The southerly gale is bitterly severe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' drops the final E of AUSTERE; the 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Auster is the Latin name for the southerly wind, personified in Roman myth.

clue.text: Himalayan porter carries her pack, partly

indicators.note: partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A mountain guide carries a woman's luggage.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherpas are Nepalese people famous for guiding and carrying loads on Himalayan expeditions.

clue.text: Poisonous plant left out of extravagant display

indicators.note: out of says one piece is taken away from the other

parts.note: a splurge is a lavish display or spending spree

explanation.surface: A toxic plant left out of a flamboyant show.
explanation.definitionFit: Spurges are plants of the euphorbia family whose milky sap is toxic.

clue.text: Strait-laced sort, with hint of puritan attire

indicators.note: a hint of a word is just its first letter

parts.note: rig is informal for clothing or outfit

explanation.surface: A prude dresses with a touch of the Puritan style.
explanation.definitionFit: A prig is a self-righteous person, smug about propriety.

clue.text: Tricks in slam Des and I contrived to make

indicators.note: contrived means artfully arranged, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Des and I fixed a bridge slam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' joins the fodder words but adds no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To mislead is to deceive or give a false impression.

clue.text: Record outstanding, Edward found

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
over means remaining or left outstanding
Ed is short for Edward

explanation.surface: Edward finds an outstanding record.
explanation.definitionFit: Discovered means came upon or found out.

clue.text: Vessel about right for wine

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: a pot is a vessel

explanation.surface: A vessel set right for some wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a ship, the port of call; it is a pot.
explanation.definitionFit: Port is a sweet fortified wine from Portugal.
